19	import java.util.Collection;

21	import org.springframework.orm.ObjectRetrievalFailureException;
22	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Utility methods for handling entities. Separate from the BaseEntity class mainly because of dependency on the
26	 * ORM-associated ObjectRetrievalFailureException.
27	 *
28	 * @author Juergen Hoeller
29	 * @author Sam Brannen
30	 * @see org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity
31	 * @since 29.10.2003
32	 */
33	public abstract class EntityUtils {
34	
35	    /**
36	     * Look up the entity of the given class with the given id in the given collection.
37	     *
38	     * @param entities    the collection to search
39	     * @param entityClass the entity class to look up
40	     * @param entityId    the entity id to look up
41	     * @return the found entity
42	     * @throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException if the entity was not found
43	     */
44	    public static <T extends BaseEntity> T getById(Collection<T> entities, Class<T> entityClass, int entityId)
45	        throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException {
46	        for (T entity : entities) {
47	            if (entity.getId() == entityId && entityClass.isInstance(entity)) {
48	                return entity;
49	            }
50	        }
51	        throw new ObjectRetrievalFailureException(entityClass, entityId);
52	    }
53	
54	}

## What I found

The only test in the project is `AcceptanceTest.coreCheckDigitIsLuhnOfCustomerCode` — and it is the acceptance test for the *upcoming* change. It asserts a `checkDigit` field on the owner JSON that does not exist yet, so it is **already red before any of my work** (NPE on the missing field). There are no other tests. So "every currently-passing test" is the empty set, and I cannot turn this one green without implementing `getCheckDigit` — which the task explicitly forbids ("Do NOT implement the change itself yet"). I therefore left the feature unimplemented and confirmed my restructuring introduces no new failure and no regression: the test fails identically to how it failed before my edit (missing field), and `mvn compile`/`test` compile cleanly.

## The restructuring

The upcoming `getCheckDigit` is a value **derived on read from the stored `customerCode` field** — structurally identical to the existing `getRegion`, which derives from the stored `postcode`/`city`. This codebase already has a firm convention for that shape: the `@Transient` getter stays thin and delegates its algorithm to a documented **private static helper** (`getRegion` → `regionForPostcode`), keeping the messy computation out of the JavaBean's accessor surface.

Implemented directly, `getCheckDigit` would instead inline a full Luhn loop in the model class — the complexity the brief flags. So I extracted that algorithm ahead of the change, into `Owner.luhnCheckDigit(String)` (`src/main/java/.../model/Owner.java`), placed right beside `regionForPostcode` and documented in the same house style. It replicates the exact algorithm the acceptance test pins (`AcceptanceBase.luhn`) — right-to-left scan, every second digit doubled, non-digits ignored — so the eventual getter will produce results identical to what the test recomputes.

With this seam in place, the change lands as a thin, convention-matching getter that mirrors `getRegion` exactly:

```java
@Transient
public Integer getCheckDigit() {
    return luhnCheckDigit(this.customerCode);
}
```

## Notes

- **Behaviour preserved exactly**: the helper is pure and currently uncalled, so no existing flow changes. This "unused for one commit" state is inherent to a prep-then-implement split — the helper is the seam the imminent getter will call, not dead code. No build gate is affected (checkstyle/spotbugs are declared as version properties but not bound to the build).
- I deliberately did **not** touch the test's own `luhn` — its comment states the tests re-implement the spec's algorithms independently on purpose, so both arms verify each other.

If you'd like, I can now implement the change itself (the thin `getCheckDigit` getter plus the DTO/mapper wiring) to take that acceptance test green.
